sanskrit: tasminn evātha kāle tu tīrthayātrām upāgataḥ ikṣvākur agamat tatra sametā yatra te vibho
english: At that very time, O lord, having undertaken a pilgrimage to the sacred fords, Ikṣvāku came there, to the place where those sages were assembled.

sanskrit: sarvān eva tu rājarṣiḥ saṃpūjyābhipraṇamya ca kuśalapraśnam akarot sarveṣāṃ rājasattamaḥ
english: That royal sage, the best of kings, honored them all and bowed before them, and inquired after the welfare of every one of them.

sanskrit: tasmai so 'thāsanaṃ dattvā pādyam arghyaṃ tathaiva ca abravīd brāhmaṇo vākyaṃ kṛtvā kuśalasaṃvidam
english: Then the brāhmaṇa, having offered him a seat, water for his feet, and the guest-offering, and having exchanged greetings of welfare, spoke these words.

sanskrit: svāgataṃ te mahārāja brūhi yad yad ihecchasi svaśaktyā kiṃ karomīha tad bhavān prabravītu me
english: "Welcome to you, great king. Tell me whatever you desire here. What may I do for you according to my power? Let your honor declare it to me."

sanskrit: rājovāca rājāhaṃ brāhmaṇaś ca tvaṃ yadi ṣaṭkarmasaṃsthitaḥ dadāmi vasu kiṃ cit te prārthitaṃ tad vadasva me
english: The king said: "I am a king, and you are a brāhmaṇa, established in the six prescribed duties. I shall give you some wealth; tell me what you would ask of me."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca dvividhā brāhmaṇā rājan dharmaś ca dvividhaḥ smṛtaḥ pravṛttaś ca nivṛttaś ca nivṛtto 'smi pratigrahāt
english: The brāhmaṇa said: "Brāhmaṇas, O king, are of two kinds, and dharma too is held to be twofold—the path of engagement and the path of withdrawal. I have withdrawn from the acceptance of gifts."

sanskrit: tebhyaḥ prayaccha dānāni ye pravṛttā narādhipa ahaṃ na pratigṛhṇāmi kim iṣṭaṃ kiṃ dadāni te brūhi tvaṃ nṛpatiśreṣṭha tapasā sādhayāmi kim
english: "Give your gifts, O ruler of men, to those who follow the path of engagement; I do not accept them. What is your wish? What may I give you? Tell me, O best of kings—what shall I accomplish for you by my austerity?"

sanskrit: rājovāca kṣatriyo 'haṃ na jānāmi dehīti vacanaṃ kva cit prayaccha yuddham ity evaṃ vādinaḥ smo dvijottama
english: The king said: "I am a kṣatriya; I know not anywhere the word 'give to me.' 'Grant me battle'—such is the speech we are wont to utter, O best of the twice-born."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca tuṣyasi tvaṃ svadharmeṇa tathā tuṣṭā vayaṃ nṛpa anyonyasyottaraṃ nāsti yad iṣṭaṃ tat samācara
english: The brāhmaṇa said: "You are content with your own dharma, and so, O king, are we content with ours. Neither has the upper hand over the other; do then as you wish."

sanskrit: rājovāca svaśaktyāhaṃ dadānīti tvayā pūrvaṃ prabhāṣitam yāce tvāṃ dīyatāṃ mahyaṃ japyasyāsya phalaṃ dvija
english: The king said: "You said before, 'I shall give according to my power.' I beg of you: let the fruit of this japa of yours be given to me, O twice-born one."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca yuddhaṃ mama sadā vāṇī yācatīti vikatthase na ca yuddhaṃ mayā sārdhaṃ kimarthaṃ yācase punaḥ
english: The brāhmaṇa said: "You boasted that your speech ever asks only for battle. Yet there is no battle between you and me—why, then, do you now ask of me at all?"

sanskrit: rājovāca vāgvajrā brāhmaṇāḥ proktāḥ kṣatriyā bāhujīvinaḥ vāgyuddhaṃ tad idaṃ tīvraṃ mama vipra tvayā saha
english: The king said: "Brāhmaṇas are said to be armed with the thunderbolt of speech, while kṣatriyas live by the strength of their arms. This, O sage, is a fierce war of words between you and me."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca saivādyāpi pratijñā me svaśaktyā kiṃ pradīyatām brūhi dāsyāmi rājendra vibhave sati māciram
english: The brāhmaṇa said: "That same pledge of mine still stands even now. What shall I give you according to my power? Tell me, O lord of kings, and I shall give it without delay, so far as my means allow."

sanskrit: rājovāca yat tad varṣaśataṃ pūrṇaṃ japyaṃ vai japatā tvayā phalaṃ prāptaṃ tat prayaccha mama ditsur bhavān yadi
english: The king said: "That fruit which you have won by reciting your prayer through a full hundred years—give that to me, if your honor is minded to give."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca paramaṃ gṛhyatāṃ tasya phalaṃ yaj japitaṃ mayā ardhaṃ tvam avicāreṇa phalaṃ tasya samāpnuhi
english: The brāhmaṇa said: "Then let the highest fruit of what I have recited be taken. Receive, without hesitation, half the fruit thereof."

sanskrit: atha vā sarvam eveha japyakaṃ māmakaṃ phalam rājan prāpnuhi kāmaṃ tvaṃ yadi sarvam ihecchasi
english: "Or rather, O king, take the whole fruit of my recitation as you wish, if it is everything that you desire here."

sanskrit: rājovāca kṛtaṃ sarveṇa bhadraṃ te japyaṃ yad yācitaṃ mayā svasti te 'stu gamiṣyāmi kiṃ ca tasya phalaṃ vada
english: The king said: "I have no need of the whole—blessings upon you. I asked only for the prayer's fruit. May it be well with you; I shall go. But tell me, what is that fruit?"

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca phalaprāptiṃ na jānāmi dattaṃ yaj japitaṃ mayā ayaṃ dharmaś ca kālaś ca yamo mṛtyuś ca sākṣiṇaḥ
english: The brāhmaṇa said: "I know not what fruit I have won; I have given what I recited. Let Dharma here, and Time, and Yama, and Death be witnesses to this."

sanskrit: rājovāca ajñātam asya dharmasya phalaṃ me kiṃ kariṣyati prāpnotu tat phalaṃ vipro nāham icche sasaṃśayam
english: The king said: "What use to me is the fruit of this merit, when its measure is unknown? Let the sage keep that fruit; I do not wish for what is uncertain."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca nādade 'paravaktavyaṃ dattaṃ vācā phalaṃ mayā vākyaṃ pramāṇaṃ rājarṣe mamāpi tava caiva hi
english: The brāhmaṇa said: "I shall not take back what I have given; the fruit has been given by my word, and a word once given may not be gainsaid. The spoken word is binding, O royal sage—upon me and upon you alike."

sanskrit: nābhisaṃdhir mayā japye kṛtapūrvaḥ kathaṃ cana japyasya rājaśārdūla kathaṃ jñāsyāmy ahaṃ phalam
english: "Never in any way did I make a calculation of gain in my recitation. O tiger among kings, how then should I know its fruit?"

sanskrit: dadasveti tvayā coktaṃ dadāmīti tathā mayā na vācaṃ dūṣayiṣyāmi satyaṃ rakṣa sthiro bhava
english: "'Give to me,' was said by you, and 'I give,' was said by me in answer. I shall not falsify my word; guard the truth, and stand firm."

sanskrit: athaivaṃ vadato me 'dya vacanaṃ na kariṣyasi mahān adharmo bhavitā tava rājan mṛṣākṛtaḥ
english: "If now you will not honor my word, spoken thus, a great unrighteousness will fall upon you, O king, wrought by your own falsehood."

sanskrit: na yuktaṃ tu mṛṣā vāṇī tvayā vaktum ariṃdama tathā mayāpy abhyadhikaṃ mṛṣā vaktuṃ na śakyate
english: "It is not fitting for you to utter a false word, O subduer of foes; and still less can I bring myself to speak falsely."

sanskrit: saṃśrutaṃ ca mayā pūrvaṃ dadānīty avicāritam tad gṛhṇīṣvāvicāreṇa yadi satye sthito bhavān
english: "I promised before, without reservation, 'I shall give.' Take it, then, without hesitation, if your honor stands in truth."

sanskrit: ihāgamya hi māṃ rājañ jāpyaṃ phalam ayācithāḥ tan mannisṛṣṭaṃ gṛhṇīṣva bhava satye sthiro 'pi ca
english: "For having come here, O king, you begged of me the fruit of my recitation. Take, then, what I have surrendered, and stand firm in truth."

sanskrit: nāyaṃ loko 'sti na paro na ca pūrvān sa tārayet kuta evāvarān rājan mṛṣāvādaparāyaṇaḥ
english: "For the man addicted to falsehood there is neither this world nor the next; he cannot deliver his forefathers—how much less, O king, his descendants?"

sanskrit: na yajñādhyayane dānaṃ niyamās tārayanti hi tathā satyaṃ pare loke yathā vai puruṣarṣabha
english: "Neither sacrifice, nor Vedic study, nor giving, nor the vows can deliver a man in the world beyond, O bull among men, as truth can."

sanskrit: tapāṃsi yāni cīrṇāni cariṣyasi ca yat tapaḥ samāḥ śataiḥ sahasraiś ca tat satyān na viśiṣyate
english: "The austerities you have already performed, and the austerity you shall yet perform through hundreds and thousands of years—none of it surpasses truth."

sanskrit: satyam ekākṣaraṃ brahma satyam ekākṣaraṃ tapaḥ satyam ekākṣaro yajñaḥ satyam ekākṣaraṃ śrutam
english: "Truth is the single-syllabled brahman; truth is the single-syllabled austerity; truth is the single-syllabled sacrifice; truth is the single-syllabled sacred lore."

sanskrit: satyaṃ vedeṣu jāgarti phalaṃ satye paraṃ smṛtam satyād dharmo damaś caiva sarvaṃ satye pratiṣṭhitam
english: "Truth keeps watch within the Vedas; the highest fruit is held to lie in truth. From truth come dharma and self-restraint; all things rest upon truth."

sanskrit: satyaṃ vedās tathāṅgāni satyaṃ yajñas tathā vidhiḥ vratacaryās tathā satyam oṃkāraḥ satyam eva ca
english: "Truth is the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences; truth is the sacrifice and its ordinance; truth too is the practice of vows; and truth is the very syllable Oṃ."

sanskrit: prāṇināṃ jananaṃ satyaṃ satyaṃ saṃtatir eva ca satyena vāyur abhyeti satyena tapate raviḥ
english: "Truth is the birth of living beings, and truth is their continuance. By truth the wind blows on its course; by truth the sun gives forth its heat."

sanskrit: satyena cāgnir dahati svargaḥ satye pratiṣṭhitaḥ satyaṃ yajñas tapo vedāḥ stobhā mantrāḥ sarasvatī
english: "By truth the fire burns; heaven is established upon truth. Truth is the sacrifice, the austerity, the Vedas, the chants, the sacred verses, and the goddess Sarasvatī."

sanskrit: tulām āropito dharmaḥ satyaṃ caiveti naḥ śrutam samāṃ kakṣāṃ dhārayato yataḥ satyaṃ tato 'dhikam
english: "Dharma and truth, so we have heard, were once set upon a balance; and while the two held the scale even, truth proved the weightier."

sanskrit: yato dharmas tataḥ satyaṃ sarvaṃ satyena vardhate kimartham anṛtaṃ karma kartuṃ rājaṃs tvam icchasi
english: "Where there is dharma, there is truth; all things grow by truth. Why, then, O king, do you wish to do an act of untruth?"

sanskrit: satye kuru sthiraṃ bhāvaṃ mā rājann anṛtaṃ kṛthāḥ kasmāt tvam anṛtaṃ vākyaṃ dehīti kuruṣe 'śubham
english: "Set your heart firmly upon truth; commit no falsehood, O king. Why do you make of your inauspicious word, 'give to me,' a thing of untruth?"

sanskrit: yadi japyaphalaṃ dattaṃ mayā neṣiṣyase nṛpa svadharmebhyaḥ paribhraṣṭo lokān anucariṣyasi
english: "If you will not receive the fruit of the recitation given by me, O king, then, fallen from your own duties, you will wander through the worlds in misery."

sanskrit: saṃśrutya yo na ditseta yācitvā yaś ca necchati ubhāv ānṛtikāv etau na mṛṣā kartum arhasi
english: "He who, having promised, will not give, and he who, having begged, will not receive—both these are men of untruth. You ought not to make yourself false."

sanskrit: rājovāca yoddhavyaṃ rakṣitavyaṃ ca kṣatradharmaḥ kila dvija dātāraḥ kṣatriyāḥ proktā gṛhṇīyāṃ bhavataḥ katham
english: The king said: "To fight and to protect—such, indeed, is the dharma of the kṣatriya, O twice-born one. Kṣatriyas are called givers; how, then, should I take from you?"

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca na chandayāmi te rājan nāpi te gṛham āvrajam ihāgamya tu yācitvā na gṛhṇīṣe punaḥ katham
english: The brāhmaṇa said: "I did not solicit you, O king, nor did I come to your house. You it was who came here and begged of me; how, then, will you now refuse to receive?"

sanskrit: dharma uvāca avivādo 'stu yuvayor vittaṃ māṃ dharmam āgatam dvijo dānaphalair yukto rājā satyaphalena ca
english: Dharma said: "Let there be no dispute between you two. Know me to be Dharma, come hither in person. The brāhmaṇa is endowed with the fruit of giving, and the king with the fruit of truth."

sanskrit: svarga uvāca svargaṃ māṃ viddhi rājendra rūpiṇaṃ svayam āgatam avivādo 'stu yuvayor ubhau tulyaphalau yuvām
english: Heaven said: "Know me, O lord of kings, to be Heaven, come here in embodied form. Let there be no dispute between you two; you both are equal in the fruit you have earned."

sanskrit: rājovāca kṛtaṃ svargeṇa me kāryaṃ gaccha svarga yathāsukham vipro yadīcchate dātuṃ pratīcchatu ca me dhanam
english: The king said: "I have no business with heaven; go, O Heaven, as you please. If the sage wishes to give, then let him in turn accept my wealth."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca bālye yadi syād ajñānān mayā hastaḥ prasāritaḥ nivṛttilakṣaṇaṃ dharmam upāse saṃhitāṃ japan
english: The brāhmaṇa said: "If in my childhood, through ignorance, I once stretched out my hand to receive, yet now I follow the dharma marked by withdrawal, reciting the sacred text."

sanskrit: nivṛttaṃ māṃ ciraṃ rājan vipraṃ lobhayase katham svena kāryaṃ kariṣyāmi tvatto necche phalaṃ nṛpa tapaḥsvādhyāyaśīlo 'haṃ nivṛttaś ca pratigrahāt
english: "Me, a brāhmaṇa long withdrawn from the world, why, O king, do you seek to tempt? I shall accomplish my purpose by my own means; I desire no fruit from you, O king. Devoted to austerity and to sacred study, I have ceased from the acceptance of gifts."

sanskrit: rājovāca yadi vipra nisṛṣṭaṃ te japyasya phalam uttamam āvayor yat phalaṃ kiṃ cit sahitaṃ nau tad astv iha
english: The king said: "If, O sage, the highest fruit of your recitation has been surrendered by you, then whatever fruit belongs to us two, let it here be held by us together."

sanskrit: dvijāḥ pratigrahe yuktā dātāro rājavaṃśajāḥ yadi dharmaḥ śruto vipra sahaiva phalam astu nau
english: "The twice-born are appointed to receive, and those born of royal lineage to give. If dharma has been truly heard by us, O sage, then let the fruit be shared by us both."

sanskrit: mā vā bhūt sahabhojyaṃ nau madīyaṃ phalam āpnuhi pratīccha matkṛtaṃ dharmaṃ yadi te mayy anugrahaḥ
english: "Or else, let there be no sharing between us: take then the fruit that is mine. Accept the merit I have wrought, if you would show me your grace."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tato vikṛtaceṣṭau dvau puruṣau samupasthitau gṛhītvānyonyam āveṣṭya kucelāv ūcatur vacaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Then two men of strange demeanor appeared, ill-clad, clutching and clinging to each other, and spoke these words.

sanskrit: na me dhārayasīty eko dhārayāmīti cāparaḥ ihāsti nau vivādo 'yam ayaṃ rājānuśāsakaḥ
english: "You owe me nothing," said the one; "I do owe you," said the other. "This is the dispute between us; let this king be our judge."

sanskrit: satyaṃ bravīmy aham idaṃ na me dhārayate bhavān anṛtaṃ vadasīha tvam ṛṇaṃ te dhārayāmy aham
english: "I speak the truth in this: you owe me nothing." "It is you who speak falsely here; I do owe a debt to you."

sanskrit: tāv ubhau bhṛśasaṃtaptau rājānam idam ūcatuḥ parīkṣyatāṃ yathā syāva nāvām iha vigarhitau
english: The two of them, both sorely troubled, said this to the king: "Let the matter be examined, so that we two may not stand here in disgrace."

sanskrit: virūpa uvāca dhārayāmi naravyāghra vikṛtasyeha goḥ phalam dadataś ca na gṛhṇāti vikṛto me mahīpate
english: Virūpa said: "O tiger among men, I owe to Vikṛta here the fruit of a cow; yet though I would pay it, Vikṛta will not accept it from me, O lord of earth."

sanskrit: vikṛta uvāca na me dhārayate kiṃ cid virūpo 'yaṃ narādhipa mithyā bravīty ayaṃ hi tvā mithyābhāsaṃ narādhipa
english: Vikṛta said: "This Virūpa owes me nothing at all, O ruler of men. He speaks falsely, and it is to you, O king, that he makes this false appearance."

sanskrit: rājovāca virūpa kiṃ dhārayate bhavān asya vadasva me śrutvā tathā kariṣyāmīty evaṃ me dhīyate matiḥ
english: The king said: "Virūpa, what is it that you owe to him? Tell me, and having heard it I shall act accordingly—such is the resolve of my mind."

sanskrit: virūpa uvāca śṛṇuṣvāvahito rājan yathaitad dhārayāmy aham vikṛtasyāsya rājarṣe nikhilena nararṣabha
english: Virūpa said: "Listen attentively, O king, how it is that I owe this to Vikṛta here, in its entirety, O royal sage, O bull among men."

sanskrit: anena dharmaprāptyarthaṃ śubhā dattā purānagha dhenur viprāya rājarṣe tapaḥsvādhyāyaśīline
english: "Long ago, O sinless one, this man, for the sake of gaining merit, gave a fine milk-cow, O royal sage, to a brāhmaṇa devoted to austerity and sacred study."

sanskrit: tasyāś cāyaṃ mayā rājan phalam abhyetya yācitaḥ vikṛtena ca me dattaṃ viśūddhenāntarātmanā
english: "And I, O king, came to Vikṛta and begged of him the fruit of that gift; and Vikṛta gave it to me with a wholly purified inner heart."

sanskrit: tato me sukṛtaṃ karma kṛtam ātmaviśuddhaye gāvau hi kapile krītvā vatsale bahudohane
english: "Thereafter I did a meritorious deed for my own purification: I bought two tawny cows, fond of their calves and abundant in milk."

sanskrit: te coñchavṛttaye rājan mayā samapavarjite yathāvidhi yathāśraddhaṃ tad asyāhaṃ punaḥ prabho
english: "And those two, O king, I bestowed, as was prescribed and with full faith, upon one who lived by gleaning. That same merit, O lord, I would now once more render back to him."

sanskrit: ihādya vai gṛhītvā tat prayacche dviguṇaṃ phalam ekasyāḥ puruṣavyāghra kaḥ śuddhaḥ ko 'tra doṣavān
english: "Having received that, I would now repay it here twofold for the one cow. O tiger among men, who in this matter is in the right, and who at fault?"

sanskrit: evaṃ vivadamānau svas tvām ihābhyāgatau nṛpa kuru dharmam adharmaṃ vā vinaye nau samādhaya
english: "Thus disputing, we two have come before you here, O king. Do what is right or what is wrong, but settle us in due conduct and resolve our quarrel."

sanskrit: yadi necchati me dānaṃ yathā dattam anena vai bhavān atra sthiro bhūtvā mārge sthāpayatu prabhuḥ
english: "If he will not accept my gift, even as this man once gave to me, then let your honor, standing firm in this, set us upon the right path, O lord."

sanskrit: rājovāca dīyamānaṃ na gṛhṇāsi ṛṇaṃ kasmāt tvam adya vai yathaiva te 'bhyanujñātaṃ tathā gṛhṇīṣva māciram
english: The king said: "Why do you not accept the debt now offered to you? Even as it has been granted to you, so receive it without delay."

sanskrit: vikṛta uvāca dīyatām ity anenoktaṃ dadānīti tathā mayā nāyaṃ me dhārayaty atra gamyatāṃ yatra vāñchati
english: Vikṛta said: "'Let it be given,' was said by him, and 'I give,' was said by me. He owes me nothing in this matter; let him go wherever he wishes."

sanskrit: rājovāca dadato 'sya na gṛhṇāsi viṣamaṃ pratibhāti me daṇḍyo hi tvaṃ mama mato nāsty atra khalu saṃśayaḥ
english: The king said: "You do not accept it though he offers—this seems to me unjust. You, I judge, deserve punishment; of that there is surely no doubt."

sanskrit: vikṛta uvāca mayāsya dattaṃ rājarṣe gṛhṇīyāṃ tat kathaṃ punaḥ kāmam atrāparādho me daṇḍyam ājñāpaya prabho
english: Vikṛta said: "I gave it to him, O royal sage; how then should I take it back again? If herein lies my offense, decree my punishment, O lord."

sanskrit: virūpa uvāca dīyamānaṃ yadi mayā neṣiṣyasi kathaṃ cana niyaṃsyati tvā nṛpatir ayaṃ dharmānuśāsakaḥ
english: Virūpa said: "If you will in no wise accept what is offered by me, then this king, the upholder of dharma, will restrain and chastise you."

sanskrit: vikṛta uvāca svaṃ mayā yāciteneha dattaṃ katham ihādya tat gṛhṇīyāṃ gacchatu bhavān abhyanujñāṃ dadāni te
english: Vikṛta said: "What was my own I gave here when begged of me; how should I take it back again today? Go, your honor—I grant you leave to depart."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca śrutam etat tvayā rājann anayoḥ kathitaṃ dvayoḥ pratijñātaṃ mayā yat te tad gṛhāṇāvicāritam
english: The brāhmaṇa said: "You have heard, O king, what these two have related. Take, then, without hesitation, what I promised to you."

sanskrit: rājovāca prastutaṃ sumahat kāryam āvayor gahvaraṃ yathā jāpakasya dṛḍhīkāraḥ katham etad bhaviṣyati
english: The king said: "A weighty matter is here laid before us two, deep as a thicket. How shall this firm resolve of the reciter be carried through?"

sanskrit: yadi tāvan na gṛhṇāmi brāhmaṇenāpavarjitam kathaṃ na lipyeyam ahaṃ doṣeṇa mahatādya vai
english: "If, then, I do not accept what the brāhmaṇa has surrendered, how shall I not today be tainted with a grievous fault?"

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tau covāca sa rājarṣiḥ kṛtakāryau gamiṣyathaḥ nedānīṃ mām ihāsādya rājadharmo bhaven mṛṣā
english: Bhīṣma said: And that royal sage said to the two: "Your purpose accomplished, you may now depart. Let it not be, now that you have come to me, that the dharma of kings should prove false."

sanskrit: svadharmaḥ paripālyaś ca rājñām eṣa viniścayaḥ vipradharmaś ca sugurur mām anātmānam āviśat
english: "One's own dharma must be upheld—such is the firm conclusion for kings. Yet the dharma of the brāhmaṇa weighs heavy; it has entered me, who am no longer master of myself."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca gṛhāṇa dhāraye 'haṃ te yācitaṃ te śrutaṃ mayā na ced grahīṣyase rājañ śapiṣye tvāṃ na saṃśayaḥ
english: The brāhmaṇa said: "Take it; I owe it to you. I have heard your request. If you will not receive it, O king, I shall surely curse you—of that there is no doubt."

sanskrit: rājovāca dhig rājadharmaṃ yasyāyaṃ kāryasyeha viniścayaḥ ityarthaṃ me grahītavyaṃ kathaṃ tulyaṃ bhaved iti
english: The king said: "Shame upon the dharma of kings, which decides such a matter thus! For this reason I must accept it—how else might the scales be made even?"

sanskrit: eṣa pāṇir apūrvaṃ bho nikṣepārthaṃ prasāritaḥ yan me dhārayase vipra tad idānīṃ pradīyatām
english: "Behold, O sir, this hand of mine is stretched out as never before, to receive the deposit. What you owe me, O sage, let it now be given."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca saṃhitāṃ japatā yāvān mayā kaś cid guṇaḥ kṛtaḥ tat sarvaṃ pratigṛhṇīṣva yadi kiṃ cid ihāsti me
english: The brāhmaṇa said: "Whatever merit I have gained by reciting the sacred text—receive it all, if indeed any merit of mine exists."

sanskrit: rājovāca jalam etan nipatitaṃ mama pāṇau dvijottama samam astu sahaivāstu pratigṛhṇātu vai bhavān
english: The king said: "This water has fallen upon my palm, O best of the twice-born. Let it be shared, let it be held in common—and let your honor too accept it."
